text:
mike: heads-up — found a deploy key in a public S3 object (logs bucket) that was accidentally made public for ~2h. Key tied to ci-deploy@redwood. Possible write access to some infra repos. :rotating_light:

security-bot: Indicator: s3://redwood-logs/ci/build-2026-03-22/step-4.log contained key. No suspicious pushes detected so far but we need rotate asap. Guidance: https://internal.redwood/sec/ci-deploy-key-playbook

dev-alejandra: Action item list: 1) revoke the access key 2) rotate new deploy key and update CI secrets 3) remove leaked key from logs and infra history 4) run forensic scan for any anomalous git pushes.

ops-ryan: Revoking now: `aws iam update-access-key --user-name ci-deploy --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive` then `aws iam delete-access-key ...` Will also disable the CI job that uses it.

sre-lin: I'll pause deploy pipelines and roll to fallback images. Canary pipelines set to manual until keys rotated.

dev-alejandra: To scrub history: run `git filter-repo --path-glob 'scripts/*' --replace-text replacements.txt` and rotate any repo deploy keys. Also remove the log object from S3 and enable object lock for logs going forward.

compliance-rosa: Please add this to the incident register with timestamps of revoke and rotation and attach Jira ticket. We need evidence for auditors.

devops-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026-999 in Jira and assigned to @dev-alejandra and @ops-ryan. Audit log entry: /ops/audit/2026/deploykey-1797003200.log

mike: Engineers: replace CI usage with OIDC where possible. If you must use a key, create a short-lived key and scope permissions to specific repos only.

ops-ryan: Forensic note: checking CloudTrail for PutObject/GetObject from unusual IPs and `git push` activity around the window 2026-03-22T14:10:00Z-2026-03-22T16:10:00Z. Will post findings.

dev-alejandra: After rotation, update repo README and CI docs to include checklist and add a pre-commit hook to block accidental key patterns. PR incoming.

security-bot: Mitigation checklist: rotate key, revoke old key, scan logs for exfil, scrub git history if leaked, enable bucket-level deny for public ACLs, migrate CI to OIDC. See https://internal.redwood/sec/ci-keys-playbook

compliance-rosa: Once complete, email compliance@redwood with: Jira ticket, revoked key id, rotation timestamp, and who approved.

mike: thanks everyone — please update this thread when done. :thumbsup:
